more_info.overview: Polyvinylpolypyrrolidone, or PVPP, is a crosslinked form of polyvinylpyrrolidone that is insoluble in common solvents. Its stabilising role is to help a food maintain its physical consistency or the distribution of its ingredients. Produced by crosslinking the polymer formed from N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone. It is a synthetic, insoluble polymer. The specified material is supplied as white powder. The specification describes it as effectively insoluble in water.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain food supplements supplied in a solid form, excluding food supplements for infants and young children; table-top sweeteners in tablets.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
